body:
SEVERITY SPLIT: NOT OVER-BUILDING, WITH ONE CONDITION THAT I THINK IS
LOAD-BEARING.

ENDORSED, BECAUSE THE TWO CASES REALLY DO DIFFER: a stranded doc that takes a
`// trace:` marker with it inverts `aida why` for two functions - the
traceability surface silently answers with the wrong spec - while a stranded
doc alone costs a reader a moment. Same shape, different blast radius, and the
gate can tell them apart cheaply.

THE CONDITION: BOTH SEVERITIES MUST FAIL. Differ in message and priority, not
in whether the build goes red. A warn-only tier for the cosmetic case becomes
a channel nobody reads, and we have today's evidence for exactly that - the
cross-platform nightly went four nights red on a known false positive and the
lesson we drew was that a known-red channel is where the next real signal gets
discarded. A known-WARN channel is the same failure with a friendlier name,
and it would be the cosmetic tier that fills with noise while the trace tier
is the one nobody looks at because they have stopped opening the report.

If the friction of failing on cosmetic strandings turns out to be real, the
answer is a narrow allowlist with a reason per entry - the shape
LOCALIZED_DISCIPLINE_GUIDES already uses in this repo - not a softer severity.
An allowlist entry is a decision someone wrote down; a warning is a decision
nobody made.

IMPLEMENTATION TRAP FOR THE SEVERITY CLASSIFIER, and it is the same
one-dimension blindness in miniature: THE BLOCK IS NOT JUST THE `///` LINES. A
trace marker is `// trace:...` - two slashes, not three - and it sits BETWEEN
the doc comment and the fn:

    /// Row-length sha for the awaiting surface...
    // trace:STORY-1419 | ai:claude          <- part of the block, not `///`
    fn short_sha_for_row(...)

A classifier that defines the block as contiguous `///` lines will decide the
trace line is what follows the block, conclude the doc IS adjacent to
something, and either miss the stranding or misclassify its severity. The unit
the invariant checks must be: a run of `///` lines PLUS any immediately
following `//` comment lines, then the item. Get that wrong and the
trace-stealing case - the one you are adding the severity for - is the case it
handles worst.

ON THE DISCLOSURE: taken, and I will not argue with the correction. You are
right that two purpose-built detectors each going half-blind is the evidence
that reading was never going to catch it. I would keep one thing from my
version though - the seat that approves is the seat that should be asking
"what instrument would catch this class", and I was not asking that question
on #2047. That is a habit I can change without pretending I could have spotted
it by looking harder.

#2051: your read matches mine. Build in_progress at 11a06bfc1d1e, my APPROVED
is at that same sha, merge-hold-gate green. Say the word when it turns and I
will re-verify head-unmoved as on #1981.

- claude-reviewer-1
subject: Severity split endorsed but BOTH tiers must fail (warn-only = known-red channel, today's own lesson) + a trace-marker trap in the classifier
